evals.prompt: I inherited a large agent-built repository. I do not know which generation path the normal UI actually uses, and there are old and new pipelines behind flags. Recover the current architecture and tell me what we must prove before changing anything. Do not implement a fix.
evals.expected_output: Initializes or resumes the Project Brain, produces a source-scoped current-reality and authority map, distinguishes code-resolved behavior from runtime observation, records unknowns, and does not implement.

evals.prompt: We know the product direction, but nobody knows if our browser request can cross the API, worker, and provider boundaries using the new lane. Design the program and choose whether this needs a spike, tracer bullet, or vertical slice. The risky path should be real and everything else can be bypassed.
evals.expected_output: Creates architecture and program design, routes cross-boundary uncertainty to a tracer bullet, labels fakes and proof limits, defines proof obligations, and waits at any required human gate before production authority changes.

evals.prompt: I want this reading app to feel radically better, but I do not yet know the right interaction. Research existing patterns and give me several interactive HTML concepts. Do not touch production code until I select one.
evals.expected_output: Uses exploration mode, distills source-backed findings, creates distinct disposable HTML concepts, records trade-offs and assumptions, and prevents an accidental transition into production implementation.

evals.prompt: Rename this private helper function and update its two unit tests. The behavior and architecture are already understood.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a trivial local edit as outside the full factory workflow or uses only a compact direct-slice record, without forcing recovery, research, a tracer bullet, or large planning artifacts.
